title: eBART (Antioch extension) difference-in-differences: pre-registered design
fixed_by: build-loop Architect, before any treated-vs-control comparison was computed
seen_before_fixing: first date with any entries per station (ANTC 2018-03-23 and PCTR 2018-04-17: pre-opening test trickles; MLPT/BERY 2019-07: test trips)
daily ANTC+PCTR entries 2018-05-20..2018-05-28 only, to confirm the opening date (single digits before, 918 on 2018-05-26)
which dates are missing in 2018-01-01..2020-02-29 (2020-01-21, 2020-02-19) and that the 46 legacy stations have every other day
that BART publishes daily OD files only from 2018 and monthly average-weekday OD workbooks back to 2001
question: Did the eBART extension to Pittsburg Center and Antioch change ridership at the nearby legacy stations, and did it bring new riders to the corridor or only move them between stations?

event.name: eBART revenue service start (Pittsburg Center, Antioch)
sources: BART OD data: first day with ANTC+PCTR entries >= 100 must be 2018-05-26 (checked by tests/local/test_causal_local.py)

excluded.COLS: Warriors left Oracle Arena for Chase Center in Sept 2019 (control-specific shock)

primary.source: marts.fct_station_daily (BART daily OD, local DuckDB) -> analysis/causal/data/station_week.csv
primary.drop_incomplete_weeks: drop every week (for all units) in which any day has no data
primary.outcome: ln(sum of entries over the 7 days)
primary.secondary_outcome: ln(sum of exits over the 7 days)
primary.corridor_unit: sum of entries (exits) over the corridor stations; a missing station-day counts as 0
primary.model: y_it = a_i + l_t + b * D_it + u_it, OLS (statsmodels), D = treated x (e >= 0)
primary.event_study_post_bins: [0,3], [4,7], ... , [88,90] (the last bin is cut at the window end)

robustness_monthly.source: BART monthly ridership workbooks (ridership_YYYY.zip, sheet 'Weekday OD') -> analysis/causal/data/station_month_weekday.csv
robustness_monthly.model: station + month fixed effects, same station sets and inference as the primary

estimands.legacy: ATT on ln weekly entries, treated_legacy pooled (equal weight per station) vs controls; post = all e >= 0
estimands.corridor: ATT on ln weekly entries of the corridor aggregate (one unit) vs controls
estimands.buffer: ATT on ln weekly entries, buffer stations pooled vs controls (spillover check)
estimands.per_station: ATT for each of PITT, NCON, CONC separately vs controls
estimands.implied_daily_entries: corridor: (post-period actual mean weekly entries) * (1 - exp(-b)) / 7, with the same transformation applied to the CI bounds

inference.cluster: CR1 cluster-robust SEs by station (statsmodels cov_type='cluster', use_t=True); reported, but not the headline, because there are only 1-4 treated clusters
inference.headline_ci: placebo (Conley-Taber style) interval: [b - q(0.975), b - q(0.025)] of the placebo estimates (numpy.quantile, linear)
inference.placebo_pool: controls only (the real treated, new, buffer and excluded stations are never placebo-treated)

placebo_draws.corridor: 10000 distinct random sets of 5 controls, summed into one placebo corridor

inference.pretrend_test: randomization p of S = sum of squared pre-bin coefficients (reference bin excluded), for legacy and corridor; the CR1 joint Wald test is reported for legacy
inference.wild_cluster_bootstrap: not used: unreliable with 1-4 treated clusters (MacKinnon and Webb 2017, 2018); randomization inference needs no new package
falsification: in-time placebo: only weeks e <= -2, fake event at week starting 2018-03-12 (e = -11), same estimands

decision_rules.moved: corridor interval contains 0 and legacy interval entirely below 0
decision_rules.caution_flag: true if the legacy or corridor pre-trend randomization p < 0.10, or the monthly corridor interval excludes 0 with the opposite sign to the weekly corridor estimate
decision_rules.no_changes_after_results: station sets, windows, bins, outcomes, draws, seed and rules are fixed by this file; any code bug fix after the first real-data run is logged in docs/DEVLOG.md with the numbers before and after

site.chart: primary weekly event study, legacy and corridor as two small panels, 95% placebo bands
site.headline: corridor and legacy effects in % (100 * (exp(b) - 1)) with 95% placebo intervals, plus the verdict sentence
